nj_roaring_rocks.blurb: Roaring Rocks is a small boulder field tucked in the Sourland Mountain Preserve in central New Jersey, one of seven bouldering zones in the preserve. It holds 13 problems, all bouldering, and the range is wide: a handful of easy lines near V0 to V2, a middle group around V3 to V5, and a few serious test pieces up to V9. The names here include Get Smart, a popular V3, and Heart Shaped Box, a well-rated V6. It is a place for an afternoon session with a couple of pads, best suited to climbers who want moderate to hard problems.

nj_ricks_rocks.blurb: Ricks Rocks is a short single-pitch cliff at the northern end of Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, reached from Blairstown by heading west on Millbrook Road toward the Kittatinny Ridge. About a dozen routes are listed, nearly all traditional leads that can also be top-roped, running from a very easy gully up to a couple of 5.11 lines, with the bulk in the 5.6 to 5.8 range. Anchors sit well back from the edge, so bring a long static line. It is quiet most of the year but sees plenty of youth and camp groups in summer. A helmet is wise because of loose rock above the clean routes.
nj_ricks_rocks.parking_note: A roadside pull-off on Millbrook Road, reached by driving west from Route 94 in Blairstown, serves as the climbers' parking.

nj_eagle_rock_reservation.blurb: Eagle Rock Reservation is a wooded county park of roughly 400 acres on the Watchung ridge in West Orange, near Montclair and Verona. The bouldering is limited to a handful of problems around a small cave-like outcrop a short walk from the pavilion, plus a modest cliff beneath the overlook. Listed lines span V1 up to the double digits, with a middle band around V3 to V5 and several hard projects at the top end. It is an urban, short-session spot, with the skyline lookout nearby, rather than a destination with big circuits.

_expect.name: Eldorado Wall aka Rad Dudes Area

nj_k_eldorado_wall_aka_rad_dudes_area.blurb: This is a trail-facing wall on Mt. Tammany in the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, the southern end of the New Jersey side. Ten routes are listed, mostly traditional with one top-rope line and one aid route, covering a broad spread from easy fourth-class and low fifth-class up to around 5.11 and 5.12. The most recognizable feature is a tall, steep arete, and a ledge partway up acts as the first belay for most multi-pitch lines, reached by a scramble ramp on the left. Top-rope setups are easy from the trail above, and the rock is steadily praised.
